body:
I am definitely looking into ways to add a benchmark system. Some ideas that have been considered is being able to assign ranks to achieving the target score at certain levels. Like L20 is intermediate L25 advanced etc. There is always the more traditional benchmark where you just define the ranks in a sort of playlist style view (maybe by just adding more metadata to a playlist).

I am planning on adding scenarios from the viscose benchmark. Many of the scenarios should be pretty trivial to recreate.

By default crosshair and theme are saved per scenario so it will restore the values you last used when starting the scenario (or if you never plated the scenario it will carry over the current settings). You can disable this behavior if you go Settings > Scenario Settings (tab) and then change theme and crosshair from "Scenario" to "Global" which means that particular setting won't be saved per scenario. Alternatively you can disable "Save settings per scenario" completely which would be like Kovaaks behavior. You can also hold "s" to bring up the quick settings menu to quickly change the crosshair / theme. Releasing "s" will save the changes you made. Similarly holding "c" allows you to use the scrollwheel to change the crosshair size. (in case you did not discover that)

For fps the value is only capped at 2k in the ui. If you open settings.json you can set whatever value you want there. I would not suggest doing that as that will take away time that could be used for updating the state / polling mouse events / detecting hits. That rate is not tied to fps and is shown as "ups" on the screen (updates per second). I capped the value to prevent people from thinking a high fps would give them better actual performance. What I have been using is 2x monitor refresh rate personally
Submitted a change to remove the cap in the settings screen. Was able to run at 30k fps which was surprising since I haven't tried that in awhile. This will go out in the next steam release.
